item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00408","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C06","C09","C05"],"selected_candidate_label":"C06","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C06 is a strong drafting-template candidate: both letters transmit proposed legislation to Congress to permit a specifically named active-duty general to occupy a civilian federal office, explain the contemplated appointment, and request expedited passage. The child's compact formulation closely tracks C06's concrete language and sequence. C09 uses similar special legislation for a named prospective appointee facing statutory restrictions, but its circumstances and drafting are less closely parallel. C05 merely urges committee action on military-personnel legislation and lacks the named-appointee exception machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Attached is a draft of legislation which would permit General George C. Marshall to serve as Secretary of Defense.","parent_excerpt":"I am attaching hereto a draft of bill to authorize the President to appoint Major General Laurence S. Kuter as a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board, without affecting his military status and perquisites.","explanation":"Both open by transmitting a draft bill designed to make a specifically contemplated civilian appointment of a named general legally possible."},{"child_excerpt":"I request that you lay this matter before your Committee with a view to obtaining early and favorable action by the Congress.","parent_excerpt":"Since it is desirable to send Major General Kuter's nomination to the Senate at an early date, I would appreciate your aid in securing the passage of the bill as soon as practicable.","explanation":"Both conclude by asking the congressional recipient to expedite the special legislation so the intended appointment can proceed."},{"child_excerpt":"However, in view of the present critical circumstances and of General Marshall's unusual qualifications, I believe that the national interest will be served best by making an exception in this Case.","parent_excerpt":"The draft of bill would provide that Major General Kuter would continue, while serving as a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board, to receive his military pay and allowances...","explanation":"The substantive machinery is the same in broad but concrete form: special legislation creates an individualized exception allowing a military officer to serve in a civilian governmental position."}]}
